newsitem.title: INDIA: India politician goes to hospital instead of trial.
newsitem.headline: India politician goes to hospital instead of trial.

text.p: A popular Indian politician who was detained last week in connection with a corruption scandal failed to appear for a court hearing on Wednesday because he was taken to hospital complaining of "uneasiness and breathlessness".
Laloo Prasad Yadav was ordered held in judicial custody for two weeks on July 30, three months after he was indicted by federal investigators in a $280 million state farm funds scandal.
Judge S.K. Lal ordered that Yadav's judicial detention be extended until August 20 because of his failure to appear.

Yadav and 54 other officials and politicians indicted in the scandal were scheduled to appear before a special court in Patna, the capital of the eastern state of Bihar, but doctors sent the judge a medical report.
"His blood pressure was high and he was experiencing problems in breathing," one cardiologist who attended Yadav on Tuesday said.
Yadav's lawyer Shakil Ahmad Khan told the judge he feared harm would befall his client, whom the federal Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) wanted to transfer to police custody.
"The CBI may liquidate him if the agency has its way and may poison him if he is remanded to police custody," Khan said.
Judge Lal set the next hearing for August 13 and ordered authorities to protect the disgraced politician in detention. "The food must be properly examined before being served to Yadav," Lal said.

Yadav, 49, was forced to quit as chief minister of Bihar, one of India's poorest states, on July 25 when his detention became imminent. His supporters have staged protests across the state and last Sunday launched a "fill the jails" campaign in solidarity with their scandal-tainted leader.
Paramilitary police reinforcements were deployed across Patna as the indicted officials were produced before the special court.
Yadav named his unschooled wife Rabri Devi as his successor. He is housed in a luxurious police guest house converted into a makeshift prison by state authorities.
